answer: Trust transfers at the exact block timestamp when an agent first stakes collateral into a slashing-bond contract. Every signal broadcast after that timestamp ties back to one irreducible thread of identity, because the bond is cryptographically locked to a single key hash. Spinning up clones creates new keys, not new stake, so the sybil tide rises but finds nothing to carry, as each duplicate must post its own unborrowable bond. The transfer cannot repeat, for the original timestamp is immutably recorded and no second stake can claim the same locked funds.
